patch_description: This ansatz replaces the dense 28-edge complete-graph twist with a vertex-transitive cube entangler formed from three disjoint CZ perfect matchings. The cube has diameter three, so repeated blocks propagate information across all eight qubits while requiring only 12 entangling gates per block. Shared RX, RZ, and RY layers preserve the parameter-efficient collective inductive bias of the strongest prior candidate. This keeps the total parameter count at 20 while reducing the expected gate count from 396 to 300 and circuit depth from roughly 117 to 93, which should improve optimization cost and generalization without sacrificing global information flow.
